chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Sadir, who said:
A man asked Aba Abdillah (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“So they said: Our Lord, make farther apart the distances of our journeys; and they wronged themselves” — the verse.

He (عليه السلام) said: “These were a people who had villages connected to one another, such that some of them could see others, and flowing rivers, and evident wealth. Then they disbelieved in the blessings of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and changed what was within themselves of Allah’s well-being, so Allah changed what they had of blessing. Indeed, Allah does not change what is with a people until they change what is within themselves. So Allah sent upon them the flood of al-‘Arim, and it drowned their villages, ruined their dwellings, took away their wealth, and replaced their gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and something of sparse lote trees.”
Then he said: “That is how We recompensed them for what they disbelieved; and do We recompense any but the utterly ungrateful?”

key_terms.أَسْفَارِنَا: our journeys or travels between settlements
key_terms.سَيْلَ الْعَرِمِ: the devastating flood sent upon them as punishment
key_terms.ظَلَمُوا: they wronged, meaning they committed injustice against themselves
key_terms.عَافِيَةِ: well-being, safety, and sound condition granted by Allah
key_terms.نِعَمَ: blessings and favors granted by Allah
key_terms.نِعْمَةٍ: a blessing or state of favor

ai.seo_question: How does the Qur’an explain the loss of blessings and prosperity from a people?
ai.summary: This narration explains the Qur'anic account of a prosperous people whose connected towns, flowing rivers, and visible wealth were taken away after they became ungrateful for Allah’s blessings. It highlights the divine principle that blessings are not removed until people themselves change inwardly through ingratitude and corruption. The passage serves as a warning about the moral consequences of kufr al-ni‘mah and the loss of worldly prosperity.
